[[File:Great hexagonal hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great hexagonal hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great hexagonal hexecontahedron''' (or '''great astroid ditriacontahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[great snub dodecicosidodecahedron]]. It is partially [[degeneracy (mathematics)|degenerate]], having coincident [[Vertex (geometry)|vertices]], as its dual has coplanar pentagrammic faces.

==Proportions==

The faces are nonconvex hexagons. Denoting the [[golden ratio]] by <math>\phi</math>, the hexagons have one angle of <math>\arccos(-\phi^{-1})\approx 128.172\,707\,627\,01^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(-\phi^{-1})\approx 231.827\,292\,372\,99^{\circ}</math>, and four angles of <math>90^{\circ}</math>. They have two long edges, two of medium length and two short ones. If the long edges have length <math>2</math>, the medium ones have length <math>1+\phi^{-3/2}\approx 1.485\,868\,271\,76</math> and the short ones <math>1-\phi^{-3/2}\approx 0.514\,131\,728\,24</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>90^{\circ}</math>.
